title: Davy Tough, George Wettling and the snare drum touch
summary: Jones names George Wettling as better than Krupa and Tough and tells young drummers to listen to the snare drum touch of the greats.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Davy Tough had fluctuated around, he had jammed around, he had hung out with everybody. But ah, I want to interject something. There's a drummer we don't mention that was better than Gene and better than Davy. George Wettling. I knew George Wettling before I knew of a Davy Tough or what have you, but he also even playing with Paul Whiteman, he was hamstrung. He didn't get a chance to play where he wanted to play because of our social conditions.
It was my pleasure to work with him and I enjoyed every moment of it. Truly a great drummer.

I used to tell all youngsters, 'I don't care what you do. You start with the snare drums; you go to the bass, the tom-toms and cymbals. Whenever you hear Zutty Singleton, whenever you hear Gene Krupa, whenever you hear George Wettling, whenever you hear Davy Tough - don't listen to nothing but the snare drum. They never got to that touch yet, not in our travels. They don't have that.
